answer: Abetment is defined as the act of instigating or aiding another person to commit an offense, where the abettor can be held liable for the act done if it is a probable consequence of their instigation (Section 51, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023). In contrast, criminal conspiracy involves an agreement between two or more individuals to commit an illegal act (Section 61(1), Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023). The key difference lies in the nature of involvement: abetment focuses on the support or encouragement of an individual act, while conspiracy emphasizes the collective agreement to engage in unlawful conduct.
summary_answer: Abetment involves instigating or aiding another to commit an act, while criminal conspiracy requires an agreement between two or more persons to commit an illegal act.
